title: Biolistic transformation of polar diatom Fragilariopsis cylindrus
author: Amanda Hopes
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.z39f8r6
materials: Microparticle bombardmdent. A PDS-1000/He biolistic microparticle delivery system (Bio-Rad Laboratories, catalog number: 1652257) was used to transform F. cylindrus. Prior to shooting autoclave the rupture disc retaining cap and microcarrier launch assembly. Wipe the particle gun inside and out with 70% ethanol. Set-up the device according to manufacturer’s instructions. Dip a rupture disc (1550 psi) into 100% isopropanol, leave to dry and assemble into the rupture disc retaining cap. Clean helium lines by firing a shot without cells and particles. Perform particle bombardment as follows: Load a rupture disc into the retaining cap and install into the assembly. Load a stopping screen and the prepared macrocarrier holder into the microcarrier launch assembly. Place the plate with the chilled cells into the chamber (at room temperature) at a flight distance of 6cm. Create a vacuum of 25 Hg in the biolistic chamber, shoot and immediately return the cells to ice. Turn the filter paper upside down to bring the cells into contact with the Aquil plate surface and incubate at 4oC for 24 hours under standard conditions to allow cells to recover before selection. Shots are carried out in triplicate.

steps.title: Prepare and pre‑chill Aquil media
steps.instruction: Prepare Aquil media supplemented with silicate as described by Price (1989); pre‑chill the media to 4 °C and keep it on ice before use.

steps.title: Inoculate and grow diatom culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate Fragilariopsis cylindrus at 5 × 10⁴ cells · ml⁻¹ into the pre‑chilled Aquil media and grow at 4 °C under continuous 24 h light.

steps.title: Make shooting and selection agar plates
steps.instruction: Prepare 1.5 % (w/v) Aquil agar plates for shooting and 0.8 % Aquil agar plates containing a final 100 µg ml⁻¹ zeocin for selection. For each plate type, prepare 2× concentrated SOW and 2× concentrated agar separately, autoclave, cool to 50 °C, mix, add Aquil nutrients, and for selection plates add zeocin from a 100 mg ml⁻¹ stock. Pour plates, allow to set, store at 4 °C and ensure they are chilled before use.

steps.title: Prepare tungsten particle suspension
steps.instruction: Weigh 60 mg M10 tungsten particles (0.7 µm, BioRad) into a sterile 1.5 mL tube, add 1 mL 100 % ethanol, vortex 3–5 min, centrifuge 12 000 rpm for 1 min, discard supernatant; repeat wash two more times with 1 mL sterile water (centrifuge 12 000 rpm 1 min each, discard supernatant). Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL sterile water, aliquot 50 µL into fresh Eppendorf tubes, vortex frequently to keep particles in suspension, and store aliquots at –20 °C for up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare CaCl₂ and spermidine stocks
steps.instruction: Make a 2.5 M CaCl₂ solution and a 0.1 M spermidine solution; store both at –20 °C (spermidine solution to be used within one month).

steps.title: Harvest exponential‑phase cells
steps.instruction: When cultures reach 5 × 10⁵–1 × 10⁶ cells · ml⁻¹, collect 5 × 10⁷ cells per shot, filter at 4 °C onto a 47 mm diameter 1.2 µm Isopore filter (Merck, catalog RTTP04700) using vacuum filtration, place the filter onto the centre of a pre‑chilled 1.5 % agar Aquil plate, keep the plate at 4 °C until shooting, then transfer to ice.

steps.title: Coat particles with plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Thaw aliquots of CaCl₂, spermidine and tungsten particles; briefly vortex tungsten particles. For five shots, combine in a 1.5 mL tube: 50 µL tungsten particles, 5 µg plasmid DNA (dissolved in 5–10 µL sterile water), 50 µL 2.5 M CaCl₂, and 20 µL 0.1 M spermidine. Vortex 1 min, centrifuge briefly, discard supernatant, add 250 µL 100 % ethanol, vortex to homogeneity, centrifuge briefly, discard supernatant, add 50 µL 100 % ethanol, vortex. Keep coated particles on ice and use within 1 hour.

steps.title: Load coated particles onto macrocarrier
steps.instruction: Sterilize macrocarriers in 70 % ethanol and air‑dry; place them into a sterilized macrocarrier holder (sterilized by 70 % ethanol or autoclave). Vortex the coated particle suspension to resuspend, pipette 10 µL onto the centre of each macrocarrier, allow to dry with the ventilation hood off (a few minutes).

steps.title: Biolistic delivery of particles
steps.instruction: Transfer the filter‑bearing plate to ice, position the dried macrocarrier in the biolistic gun, and fire the particles onto the cells according to standard settings.

steps.title: Rinse and plate cells on selective media
steps.instruction: While keeping the plate on ice, rinse cells from the filter with 500 µL–1 mL chilled Aquil media, distribute the suspension evenly among five zeocin‑containing selective plates kept on ice, and spread with a sterilized Drigalski spatula.

steps.title: Incubate and screen transformants
steps.instruction: Incubate the selective plates at 4 °C under standard light conditions; colonies typically appear after 3–7 weeks. Screen colonies by PCR or transfer them to liquid media for further growth.
